claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and your children.

Let me start with the first question:

**Do you have any children under the age of 16, or any children aged 16-19 who are in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have one child - Alex, who is 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 16 years old, I need to understand their current situation better.

**Is Alex currently in approved education or training (such as school, college, university, or an apprenticeship)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex actually left school recently, but they've just signed up with the careers service to figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful to know. Since Alex has left education or training but has registered with a careers service, they may still be eligible for Child Benefit for a limited period.

**When exactly did Alex leave school and register with the careers service - was this within the last 20 weeks?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's been quite recent - definitely within the last 20 weeks.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for clarifying that. Now I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Do you live with Alex, or does Alex live with someone else?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect. Now I have a clearer picture. Let me ask one more important question:

**Are you the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex, or is there another person (such as Alex's other parent) who might also be claiming or planning to claim Child Benefit for them?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm the only one claiming - nobody else is getting Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me review your situation:

- You have one child, Alex, who is 16 years old
- Alex recently left school but has registered with a careers service
- This registration happened within the last 20 weeks
- Alex lives with you
- You are the only person claiming Child Benefit for Alex

Based on the Child Benefit rules, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service. Since Alex has done exactly this and it's within the 20-week window, this eligibility period applies to you.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex!** 

You can claim Child Benefit for 20 weeks from when Alex registered with the careers service. After this 20-week period ends, you would no longer be eligible unless Alex returns to approved education or training, or starts an apprenticeship.

If you haven't already done so, you'll need to make a claim with HMRC to start receiving Child Benefit payments. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
